rationale: The multi-voter execution landed with two results worth recording. First, the declared comparisons came back unknown, but only through a declaration defect: the result events did not carry the snapshots field that the applicability conditions referenced, so neither admission could be completed. Second, the controller's run shows the consequence that the earlier native probe had failed to reproduce: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the restarted node rebuilt the snapshot's three-voter configuration (event 15: after_latest_index 1, after_servers 3 against expected 14 and 5), and after being isolated with one committed voter it became leader with two votes while the committed five-voter configuration requires three and the majority side still held its own leader (event 16: became_leader true, leader_below_committed_quorum true, majority_side_leader true). The flag-off control kept the five-voter configuration and did not win (events 18 and 19). Both checks were pre-declared in this question's discriminator, so the successor experiment re-declares them with the applicability fields now emitted on the result events and re-executes the whole scenario; the current receipt is cited as raw observation, not as a completed comparison. Nothing else is restated.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is empty stays a Follower and never campaigns: the latest configuration is empty, so runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and quorumSize() returns one, while the same node restarted without the flag rebuilds the committed configuration and returns to Leader.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter configuration bootstrapped in the log, Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot so the startup configuration scan starts above the committed configuration entry; observed over a 1500 ms window with a 50 ms election timeout.

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 63a30ed680b741199ddd7877237d5874 (exit 0, twenty events, no parse loss) shows both the configuration loss and its decision-formation consequence, though its declared comparisons again returned unknown: the applicability conditions referenced a snapshots field that the result events did not carry, so the admissions could not complete ('Missing identity or applicability fields: snapshots'). The raw events are explicit. Configuration: after restarting the leader of a five-voter cluster whose snapshot carries the three-voter bootstrap configuration, event 15 reports after_latest_index 1 and after_servers 3 against expected_latest_index 14 and expected_servers 5 (config_matches false), while the flag-off control (event 18) reports index 14 with five servers. Decision formation: after the restarted node is isolated together with one committed voter, event 16 reports became_leader true with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3 and leader_below_committed_quorum true, while majority_side_leader is also true, i.e. a leader elected on a minority of the committed configuration coexists with the majority-side leader; the control (event 19) reports became_leader false. Source: with the stale configuration, quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) returns two for the three-server list and electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) counts only the votes of that list, so the node's own vote plus one follower suffices; with the committed five-server configuration the same two votes are short of the required three. The configuration loss itself comes from the parent mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied past the committed configuration before the scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read. Because the receipt's comparisons are unknown, this is recorded as conditional with the defect asserted, and a successor experiment that emits the missing applicability field and declares both checks with their controls is submitted for fresh execution; the earlier native probe's failure to reproduce the minority leader is retained as a schedule-sensitive negative.
counterevidence: The flag-off control in the same receipt keeps the five-voter configuration and does not win an election on the isolated side (events 18 and 19), isolating the recovery path.

A native construction probe of the same scenario did not produce the minority leader, and a four-voter variant left the majority side without a leader; the consequence therefore depends on the cluster size and timing, which the successor re-executes.
limitations: The comparisons in the cited receipt are unknown, so no completed comparison is claimed here.
Only the leadership decision is observed; whether the minority leader then commits an entry the majority side contradicts is not witnessed.
The election outcome appeared in the controller's run but not in the native probe, so reproducibility across schedules is not established.

experiment.revision_reason: The result events now carry the snapshots field referenced by the applicability conditions (the previous declaration could not complete for that reason), and the election check that this question's discriminator pre-declared is now expressed as a comparison with its own control. The scenario, inputs, sizes and both modes are unchanged.

scope.description: Boot three voters with RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogs, disable automatic snapshots and take exactly one snapshot while the configuration is the bootstrap one, add two voters so the committed configuration has five servers, commit more entries, restart the node that was leading from its own stores, compare the configuration it holds with the log's latest configuration, then isolate it together with one committed voter while the remaining three voters keep a majority, and report whether it becomes leader and whether that side still has a leader. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The single deliberate snapshot carries only the bootstrap configuration.
Automatic snapshots are disabled so no newer snapshot covers the change.
The isolated node and its partner hold two votes, while the committed five-voter configuration requires three.
excluded: Claims about data loss after the minority leadership; only the leadership decision and the coexistence with the majority-side leader are observed.

experiment.prefix: The harness uses MakeClusterCustom(Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs, RestoreCommittedLogs), ten Apply calls, an explicit Snapshot(), MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged with FullyConnect plus two AddVoter calls, ten more Apply calls, then Shutdown and NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores with a fresh inmem transport and FullyConnect on the rewired transports. It emits a startup_before_restart event with the snapshot index, the snapshot's configuration index, the expected configuration index and server count, then multivoter_after_restart, then multivoter_partition_election after Partition isolates the restarted node plus one committed voter; every event carries the mode, snapshots and restore flag fields used by the declarations, and no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the membership view a node resumes with: enabling RestoreCommittedLogs must not let a snapshot-age configuration decide an election that the committed configuration would refuse.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's configuration index and server count are expected to match the log's latest configuration; the defect prediction is that it falls back to the snapshot's configuration.

An election on the isolated side must not produce a leader whose support is below the committed configuration's quorum; the defect prediction is that such a leader appears while the majority side keeps its own leader.
Control: the identical restart without the flag is expected to keep the five-server configuration.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt, the isolated side cannot reach the committed quorum and must not produce a leader.
